proposal.name: Return sandbox test results within the tool limit

plan.name: Return sandbox test results within the tool limit
plan.summary: Keep the agent's test tool and the factory's checks on the same Sandbox.Run path, using an embedded Python standard-library runner that builds each touched package's test binary once, serially, discovers Test, Fuzz and Example entries, records each top-level test's elapsed time in the supplied build cache shared by one build's runs, and lets eight concurrent workers pull one top-level test at a time from a shared queue ordered with unrecorded tests first in package/name order and recorded tests longest-first (ties in package/name order), treating cache records as untrusted ordering hints, ignoring malformed or invalid data and including each discovered test exactly once in that queue, reusing the binaries from their package directories for discovery, tests and the later acceptance phase. Retain the pinned offline container, localhost hostname, isolated shared build cache, 4 GiB and 1024 process limits per container (12 GiB and 3072 processes for three watcher steps), and one-package compilation with GOMAXPROCS=2; bound the entire Run from entry by twelve minutes and the shared touched-test phase by ten minutes without resetting that budget for each test, give every inner phase and invocation its remaining time, stop subprocesses and remove the container on whole-run expiry, and reserve another minute for startup and fifteen seconds for cleanup for a total budget of thirteen minutes fifteen seconds below both unchanged 900-second backend tool limits. Return package-qualified passed, failed, running and unstarted results with names in the summary, fail on a failed build, worker, timeout or interruption while independent work continues within the remaining budget, derive Accepted from each acceptance test's own outcome, make Check reject any already-passing test or deadline, interruption or unfinished acceptance evidence while retaining completed test or build failures as evidence, and escape marker-looking stdout and stderr from every subprocess so diagnostics cannot forge runner records. Update SPEC.md and README.md to describe the system's queue ordered by recorded test durations, limits for cold runs, deadline reports and acceptance evidence without one-time merger instructions, cite D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0113, D-0117, D-0122, D-0173, D-0189, D-0197 and D-0233 as applicable in changed SPEC bullets, and adapt the existing marker-ordering fixture for compiled binaries while preserving its ordering assertions and the existing legacy-result fixtures. This policy needs a new decision recorded by the merger, whose work also includes reloading the watchers and running INVARIANT_PLUMBING_REAL=1 go test ./internal/plumbing -run '^TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout$' -count=1 -timeout 45m to require two simultaneous cold-cache real-image runs to pass and three to return within the deadline budget with named partial results allowed, measuring memory and process peaks below the enforced limits in both waves; the external plumbing_test budget test returns normally when the real-image gate is off and names internal/verify/verify.go only in its inner plan so this change's own checks touch only internal/plumbing.

tests.name: TestSandboxShardsEveryTopLevelTestExactlyOnce
tests.says: Each touched package is compiled once before workers start, and its binary is reused from its package directory for discovery, tests and acceptance checks; real tests, examples and fuzz seeds run exactly once through eight simultaneous queue workers, with subtests intact, new tests included, empty packages allowed and the chosen container limits enforced.

tests.name: TestSandboxNamesFailuresFromEveryShard
tests.says: An assertion failure, panic, worker timeout or package build error fails the check and names the failed package, test and worker where applicable, while healthy work and independent acceptance checks still complete.

tests.name: TestSandboxDeadlineReturnsPartialResults
tests.says: The sandbox's own deadline stops hung tests, vet or acceptance checks and removes the container, returning a failed result with completed, failed, running and unstarted tests distinguished and their names retained in the delivered summary.

tests.name: TestSandboxKeepsAcceptanceResultsByPackage
tests.says: Acceptance tests with the same function name in different packages retain their individual outcomes, so another package's passing test cannot satisfy a failing acceptance test.

tests.name: TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout
tests.says: The twelve-minute sandbox deadline, ten-minute test phase and one-minute startup and fifteen-second cleanup reserves stay below every supported backend tool limit; the external plumbing_test test returns normally with its real-image gate off, and its opt-in inner plan reaches internal/verify, requires two concurrent cold-cache runs to pass and three to return within budget with named partial results allowed, and measures memory and process peaks within the enforced caps in both waves.

tests.name: TestSandboxWorkersPullFromSharedQueue
tests.says: A free worker takes queued work while another worker is busy, so a test is never stranded in a fixed shard behind a long test.

tests.name: TestSandboxQueueBudgetDoesNotRestartPerTest
tests.says: All eight workers share one touched-test-phase budget; finishing a test does not restart it, and timeout preserves completed and unstarted results while acceptance checks still have time to run.

tests.name: TestSandboxAcceptanceResultsArePerTestWithinPackage
tests.says: Passing and failing acceptance tests in the same package keep their own outcomes, and Check rejects the plan because the passing test already passes on the base code.

tests.name: TestSandboxCheckRejectsDeadlineEvidence
tests.says: Check refuses deadline or interrupted runs in vet, tests and acceptance, even after acceptance tests have reported failures, while completed test failures and compiler failures for new APIs remain valid evidence.

tests.name: TestSandboxCheckRejectsUnfinishedAcceptance
tests.says: Check refuses acceptance tests recorded as not_run or running even when the process exits before the deadline.

tests.name: TestSandboxKeepsToolOutputOutsideRunnerRecords
tests.says: Vet, compilation and discovery stdout and stderr remain diagnostics; marker-looking lines and replayed runner records cannot alter test results or appear unescaped as runner records.

tests.name: TestSandboxBoundsEveryPhaseInsideContainer
tests.says: The runner itself bounds vet, compilation, discovery and acceptance by the time left and returns failed partial results without depending on host Docker cancellation.

tests.name: TestSandboxReusesMeasuredTimesInSharedCache
tests.says: A run records top-level elapsed times in its supplied build cache, and the next run in that cache starts the previously slowest known test before shorter known tests.

tests.name: TestSandboxQueuesUnknownBeforeLongestKnownTests
tests.says: The shared queue schedules tests with no valid timing first in package/name order, then known tests longest-first.

tests.name: TestSandboxTimingHintsCannotChangeInventoryOrVerdicts
tests.says: Malformed or hostile cached timing hints can only affect order: every discovered test still runs exactly once per required phase, no test or result is injected, and actual ordinary and individual acceptance verdicts are preserved.

usage.summary: Revised `plan.json` and acceptance tests for the larger deadlines and cached-duration scheduling, preserving the other agreed requirements. Check passed: all 15 acceptance tests fail on the baseline as required, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
